alternate_names: Department of Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness
notes: Federal department responsible for coordinating national security policy, cyber security strategy, critical infrastructure resilience, counter-terrorism strategy, and emergency management across the Government of Canada. Established under the Department of Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness Act (S.C. 2005, c. 10).

data.official_name: Canada's National Cyber Security Strategy
alternate_names: Securing Canada's Digital Future: Canada's National Cyber Security Strategy
Stratégie nationale de cybersécurité du Canada
data.description: Government of Canada flagship national strategy for cyber security across federal, provincial/territorial, critical infrastructure, private-sector, and international domains (editions published in 2010, 2018, and 2025).
data.notes: Three editions have been issued by Public Safety Canada: 2010 ('Canada's Cyber Security Strategy: For a Stronger and More Prosperous Canada'), 2018 ('National Cyber Security Strategy: Canada's Vision for Security and Prosperity in the Digital Age'), and February 2025 ('Securing Canada's Digital Future: Canada's National Cyber Security Strategy'). Supported by multi-year National Cyber Security Action Plans, mid-term reviews, and horizontal program evaluations.

match_nodes.description: Our Security, Our Rights: National Security Green Paper, 2016

data.official_name: Our Security, Our Rights: National Security Green Paper, 2016
alternate_names: Notre sécurité, nos droits : Livre vert sur la sécurité nationale, 2016
data.description: Comprehensive federal consultation paper reviewing Canada's national security framework, accountability institutions, intelligence powers, and cyber/counter-terrorism policy prior to the National Security Act, 2017.
data.notes: Published September 2016 to launch Canada's wide-ranging national security framework consultation; followed by the 2017 What We Learned Report and the enactment of the National Security Act, 2017 (Bill C-59).

data.notes: Published May 2017 by Public Safety Canada.
